question_text: What is implantation, with reference to embryo?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What happens
steps.why: The embryo has no food supply of its own, so it must attach to the uterine wall to reach the mother's blood.
common_mistakes: Writing that the embryo attaches to the fallopian tube. It attaches to the uterus.
steps.memory_tip: The embryo plants itself in the uterine wall.
lines: Implantation is an event early in human
pregnancy in which the embryo attaches to

steps.label: When it happens
steps.why: It takes about six days for the embryo to travel down the tube and reach the uterus.
common_mistakes: Saying it happens immediately after fertilisation.
steps.memory_tip: About the sixth day after fertilisation.

lines.text: It occurs after the 6th day of fertilisation

insider_note: Say WHEN as well as what. The sixth day after fertilisation is the detail that separates a full answer from a bare definition.
